module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1068

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/1068](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1068)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Cardinal SimpleGraph

namespace Erdos1068

/--
Does every graph with chromatic number $\aleph_1$ contain a countable subgraph which is
infinitely connected?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_1068 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (V : Type) (G : SimpleGraph V), G.chromaticCardinal = ℵ_  1 →
      ∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1068

reformulations.difference: The source asks for a 'countable subgraph which is infinitely vertex-connected' (Bowler–Pitz: 'countably infinite, infinitely connected subgraph'). The Lean asks for an INDUCED subgraph `G.induce s` on a set `s` that is merely `Set.Countable` (so finite sets are allowed). 'Infinitely many pairwise vertex-disjoint paths' becomes an infinite set of paths that are pairwise internally disjoint (`List.Disjoint` of `support.tail.dropLast`), with an extra `Nontrivial` requirement.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: (1) Induced vs. arbitrary subgraph. `InfinitelyConnected` is monotone when edges are added on the same vertex set. `Walk.mapLe` keeps the support, so it preserves being a path, injectivity on walks and internal disjointness; `Nontrivial` is unchanged. So an infinitely connected subgraph H with countable vertex set S gives an infinitely connected `G.induce S`, and an induced subgraph is itself a subgraph. (2) Countable vs. countably infinite. A finite graph has only finitely many u–v paths, and `InfinitelyConnected` requires two distinct vertices. So `s` must be infinite, as in the source's intended 'countably infinite'. The `Nontrivial` clause only rules out the degenerate 0/1-vertex case, which would make the problem trivially 'yes'. (3) All u–v paths share u and v, so 'pairwise vertex-disjoint' can only mean internally disjoint. In Lean I proved: `(∃ s : Set V, s.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected (G.induce s)) ↔ (∃ H : G.Subgraph, H.verts.Countable ∧ InfinitelyConnected H.coe)`; the full right-hand side of the theorem is unchanged under this swap; no finite graph is `InfinitelyConnected`; and `InfinitelyConnected (⊤ : SimpleGraph ℕ)` holds.

review.notes:
No defects found. The file has one declaration, `erdos_1068`.

- **Faithfulness.** The statement follows erdosproblems.com/1068. The answer slot is a Prop, the right-hand side is the positive form of the question, and there is no negation.
- **Definitions.** `chromaticCardinal` is the true cardinal chromatic number: its `sInf` is over a nonempty set, since colouring by `V` itself always works. `ℵ_ 1` is `aleph 1 = ℵ₁`, which I checked with `rfl`. `InfinitelyConnected` already contains the `Nontrivial` fix from PR #3642, so it is not satisfied vacuously by the empty or a one-point set.
- **Satisfiability.** The hypothesis can be met in `Type`: the complete graph on a type of cardinality ℵ₁ has `chromaticCardinal = ℵ_ 1` (proved in scratch). The conclusion is not trivial: known facts (no forced K_{ω,ω}; H_{ω,ω+1} has vertices of finite degree) do not settle it.
- **ℵ₁ vs. "uncountably chromatic".** Bowler–Pitz and Soukup pose the question for "uncountably chromatic" graphs; Soukup writes "(or ω₁-chromatic)". The cited source, erdosproblems.com, says "chromatic number ℵ₁", and the Lean follows it exactly. The two readings are not obviously equivalent, because a graph of chromatic number above ℵ₁ need not contain a subgraph of chromatic number exactly ℵ₁. A "yes" to the uncountable version implies a "yes" to this one. Maintainers could add the uncountable version as a variant, but this is not a defect with respect to the cited source.
- **Universe.** `V : Type` quantifies over Type 0. This is the repository's usual convention, also used in 1067.
- **Docstring.** It says "infinitely connected", following the wording before the source's Jan 2026 edit; the source now says "infinitely vertex-connected". The Lean definition is vertex connectivity (internally disjoint paths), which is the version the source calls open. The edge-connectivity version was settled by Thomassen. So the mathematics is correct; adding "vertex-" to the docstring would only be a clarity improvement.
- **Status.** `research open` matches the source: erdosproblems.com shows OPEN, the teorth data says "open", and my arXiv searches found no resolution.
- **Scratch files** (all compile): `/workspace/review/test1.lean` (K_ℕ is infinitely connected; finite and one-point graphs are not), `test2.lean` (monotonicity; induced ↔ `Subgraph` equivalence; equivalence of the full right-hand side), `test3.lean` (the hypothesis is satisfiable).
